author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory, reached at GET /specialties.html, lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name, on a single unpaginated page.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on a single page with no pagination
given a specialty held by veterinarians, when the specialty directory is opened, then each holder is listed under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under no specialty
given a veterinarian holding two specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under each of them (edge case 1)
given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the specialty directory is opened, then the specialty is still listed with no veterinarian beneath it (edge case 2)
given the specialty directory page, when it is rendered, then it carries the standard navigation required by REQ-SYS-001 and its wording is translated in every supported language per REQ-LANG-002
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged per the owner's decision)
a navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory (owner: 'A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request')
searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians (NG-9)
notes: Grounded in intake-decision line 1. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records. Boundary check: NG-2 unchanged and the page is read-only per the quoted decision; NG-9 does not apply, since this is a listing, not a search; REQ-SYS-001 means the new page carries the existing navigation, while 'no navigation entry' means nothing points to it. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions and left unrequired (narrowest reading): ordering of specialties and holders; whether an unheld specialty shows a 'none' marker; a future visible entry point. Tests should assert membership, not order. file_targets are best-effort: whether the page lives in the vet package or a new controller is a design choice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet-package pattern (controller depends on Spring Data repositories directly, Thymeleaf view under templates/vets/; system-design.md § Overview, § Contracts). Adjustment: a new read-only SpecialtyRepository in the vet package, because an unheld specialty (edge case 2) cannot be derived from vets. Specialty has no inverse association, and adding one would create a serialization cycle on the /vets route. VetController gains GET /specialties.html, which builds the specialty directory as a read projection. The projection takes every specialty from SpecialtyRepository and the cached VetRepository.findAll() collection, and inverts the holding relation keyed by specialty identifier. It constrains no domain state, so the architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog Web controller row is not engaged (recorded in system-design.md § Contracts invariants). New § Scale and Load section with its first row. Covering code resolved by ls/cat of src/main/java/.../vet/ (no IDE oracle connected; grep/read is the weaker basis): VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty present; no SpecialtyRepository exists; BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html binds no request parameter and no model attribute: binding target is none. The handler takes only Model, with no page parameter, and no @InitBinder is needed (security-principles § Mass assignment applies to request-bound types; none exists here)

Repository boundary, SpecialtyRepository: hand-written in-memory double (a small class implementing the interface) registered as a bean in VetControllerTests' @WebMvcTest context, e.g. via @Import of a @TestConfiguration (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: hand-write first). A @MockitoBean for SpecialtyRepository is not sanctioned

Repository boundary, VetRepository: the existing @MockitoBean stub in VetControllerTests stays and the new tests stub findAll() through it. This is a conscious framework-stub exception: the class has one VetRepository bean shared with the existing tests, and replacing it would rewrite those tests, which testing-principles § Mocking Policy says may stay

HTTP transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned harness, CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy). Tests assert rendered content (specialty names, 'First Last' holder names, absence of a no-specialty vet), not only model attributes

View: templates/vets/specialtyList.html uses fragments/layout with a menu argument matching no existing menu item, so the standard navigation renders (REQ-SYS-001) with no entry for this page (owner decision, intake line 1). Holder name renders as firstName + ' ' + lastName, as vetList.html does

Messages: prefer the existing keys (specialties, vets, name, none). Any new key goes into every bundle under src/main/resources/messages/ in the same change; I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces REQ-LANG-002. Stored specialty names are rendered as stored, not translated (prd-entry non-goal)

patterns.description: read-only Spring Data repository for a lookup value; shape for SpecialtyRepository (Repository<Specialty, Integer>, @Transactional(readOnly = true) finder)
controller composes model attributes from repository reads and returns a view name; the new handler follows it with no pagination helper
layout fragment usage and first-then-last name rendering

risks.risk: Grouping by Specialty entity identity fails: vets come from the cached VetRepository collection, specialties from a separate SpecialtyRepository read, and BaseEntity defines no value equality, so the same specialty appears as distinct instances (system-design.md § Contracts invariants)
risks.mitigation: Key the projection by specialty identifier. A test builds the vet's Specialty and the repository's Specialty as distinct instances sharing an id

risks.risk: Specialty directory path scales with specialties and holdings (system-design.md § Scale and Load, specialty directory row)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form per the row: one pass over the veterinarians into an insertion-ordered map keyed by specialty identifier, standard collections only. No per-specialty query and no hand-written structure

risks.risk: Cached vets and uncached specialties can disagree after an out-of-band data change (system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5)
risks.mitigation: Accepted for this slice. A holding whose specialty identifier is absent from the specialty list is dropped, not rendered under a phantom heading. Cache policy stays the open question it already is

risks.risk: Tests over-specify order or a 'none' marker, which the PRD leaves open (docs/prd.md Open Questions)
risks.mitigation: Tests assert membership and absence only, not order and not a marker for an unheld specialty. The design imposes no order

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Scoping: one behavior, one bounded context (vet); no re-split. Open questions (narrowest reading, no owner answer available): (1) presentation order of specialties and holders is unspecified by PRD and design; whatever order the repository and the vet collection yield is acceptable. (2) Whether an unheld specialty carries a 'none' marker is open; rendering the existing #{none} key is permitted but not required or tested. (3) 'Specialty directory' is now PRD vocabulary but absent from docs/ubiquitous-language.md; flagged for product-requirements-expert, not written here (not a foundational path). Controller placement follows the prd-entry file_targets (VetController); a separate controller was not chosen. No ADR: the choice has no cross-slice trade-off a later reader would re-open. docs/system-design.md writes: Package Structure vet line (repositories); Contracts rows Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, VetController gain REQ-VET-003; new SpecialtyRepository row; the specialty-directory placement invariant; new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row. Doctor check green.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No request-derived input reaches the new route: showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model) at VetController.java takes no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, or @ModelAttribute. So no mass-assignment, injection, or path-traversal row in docs/security-principles.md applies, and the change adds no binding target that would need an id disallow-list.

Output escaping is kept: specialtyList.html renders stored names only through th:text (`th:text="${entry.key.name}"`, `th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}"`), the same way the neighbouring vetList.html renders them. `grep -n -F "th:utext" -r src/main/resources/templates` returns no hits. The new template uses no __${...}__ preprocessing, no inline script, and no remote resources.

Data access goes only through the derived Spring Data method SpecialtyRepository.findAll() (`@Transactional(readOnly = true)`), with no query text and no write method. It reads Specialty, which is reference data the application has no write path for.

Exposed surface: the change adds one unauthenticated read-only GET (/specialties.html). It exposes specialty names and vet names, which /vets.html and /vets already publish to every caller. No management exposure changes, so the change is no weaker than the demonstration baseline in system-design.md Security Context.

Concurrency and the shared cache: buildSpecialtyDirectory builds request-local maps and lists, and the controller adds no mutable field. The cached Vet objects from VetRepository.findAll() (`@Cacheable("vets")`) are only read: Vet.getSpecialties() returns a fresh sorted copy (`.collect(Collectors.toList())`), so the projection cannot corrupt the shared vet cache.

Resource use: the single unpaged page is linear in specialties plus holdings over reference data, as the design's new Scale and Load row records. It allocates nothing beyond the existing unpaged /vets route, which already materializes the full vet collection.
No secrets in the diff: the change set holds no credential, token, key, or connection string.

Supply chain: the diff does not touch build.gradle or pom.xml (`git diff --stat HEAD -- build.gradle pom.xml` is empty). Resolved runtimeClasspath from `./gradlew dependencies`: spring-boot-thymeleaf 4.1.1, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -n -i "dependencycheck\|owasp" build.gradle` has no hits), so no NVD match ran in this review.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Everything sits in the vet package: one new read-only repository with a single findAll, one new GET route with no request parameters, one new template that reuses existing message keys, and doc edits that match the design block. VetController gains a constructor argument, but nothing in src constructs it by hand. No sensitive paths are touched.

semantic_surprise.note: I read buildSpecialtyDirectory hunk by hunk. It builds an insertion-ordered map with one entry per stored specialty, then makes one pass over the vets matched by specialty id. Holdings whose specialty is no longer stored are dropped, and an unheld specialty keeps an empty list. Keying the outer map by entity identity is safe because each specialty instance is inserted once. The template renders first name, a space, then last name through th:text. Nothing here does more than the diff suggests.

test_adequacy.note: The round-2 fix moved every directory assertion off the rendered HTML and onto the specialtyDirectory model attribute. performDirectory then builds the full name itself with getFirstName() + " " + getLastName(), so the rendering in specialtyList.html is no longer asserted. That rendering is what Done-when bullet 2 promises (first name then last name, shown on the page). A template that printed last-first, or left the holder cell empty, would still pass. The grouping, multi-holding, unheld and dropped-holding logic is covered by real ids and separate instances.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers on the roster approved round 2. Two approvals still carry residue. The test-reviewer's late-round recommendations say the one-page test depends on a copied page size (6 against the private size 5) and that ordering is untested. The doc-reviewer's clarify is still open: 'Specialty directory' has no ubiquitous-language entry, and I confirmed that with grep. The cited system-design.md:80 and prd.md:133 both resolve.

scope_deviation.note: The change matches the intake and PRD bullets: a read-only page reached by URL only, with no navigation entry added (the layout menu list is unchanged) and no write path. The fix round changed only the test file. There were no design revisions, consultations or build retries.

rationale: The production logic is small and correct as read. The residual risk is in the tests: the round-2 fix asserts on the model and recomputes the full name itself, so the template's first-then-last rendering is unverified. Open the page or read specialtyList.html line 20, and decide on the open glossary clarify, before merging.
